title: A finite-dimensional domain over a field is a field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $B$ a commutative $K$-algebra which is an integral domain ($1\neq0$ in $B$ and $B$ has no zero divisors) and finite-dimensional as a $K$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Then $B$ is a field: every nonzero $b\in B$ has an inverse in $B$ (multiplication by $b$ is an injective $K$-linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $B$, hence surjective, so $by=1$ for some $y\in B$).

source.place: standard (rank–nullity); used in the proof of lem-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-scalar-descent; Mathlib fieldOfFiniteDimensional
